recipes.name: Strawberry Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 2 (10 ounce) packages frozen sweetened sliced strawberries, thawed and drained

steps.text: To make the crust: Combine graham cracker crumbs, butter, sugar, and cinnamon in a bowl; mix well. Press onto the bottom of an ungreased 9-inch springform pan. Place in the refrigerator to chill for 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
To make the filling: Place strawberries and cornstarch into a blender; cover and puree until smooth.

Pour strawberry sauce into a saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil and stir until sauce is thick and shiny, about 2 minutes. Set aside 1/3 cup strawberry sauce; cool. Cover and refrigerate remaining sauce for serving.

Beat cream cheese in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; gradually beat in condensed milk. Mix in lemon juice and vanilla extract, then beat in eggs on low speed until just combined.
Pour 1/2 of the cream cheese mixture over crust; drop 1/2 of the reserved strawberry sauce by 1/2 teaspoonfuls on cream cheese layer.
Carefully spoon remaining cream cheese mixture over sauce; drop remaining strawberry sauce by 1/2 teaspoonfuls on top.
Cut through the top layer only with a knife to swirl strawberry sauce.
Bake in the preheated oven until the center is almost set, 45 to 50 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Carefully run a knife around the edge of the pan to loosen; cool for 1 hour at room temperature. Refrigerate at least 4 hours to overnight before serving.
Serve reserved strawberry sauce with cheesecake. If sauce is too thick, stir in water.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This creamy strawberry cheesecake has a crisp graham cracker crust and swirls of sweet strawberry sauce baked without a water bath for a dreamy dessert.

video.description: This creamy strawberry cheesecake is perfect for any special occasion! The beautiful purple-red color cuts through the white, and looks just as amazing as it tastes! A fruit filling offers this rich dessert a refreshing addition to such a decedent treat. Enjoy on your own, or take it with you to your next gathering.

review.reviewBody: This is a great cheesecake recipe! Very creamy and delicious. A couple suggestions: only use 1/2 a teaspoon of cinnamon as it is a very potent spice and 2 whole teaspoons makes the crust extremely sweet. You can also use natural unsweetened strawberries either frozen or fresh and the cheesecake tastes just as good!

This cheesecake is PHENOMENAL!! Oh my gosh it's sooo good! Creamy, decadent, not-to-sweet, and the little hit of strawberry takes it over the top. I have never made a cheesecake using sweetened condensed milk before, and I think I'm a convert! The resulting smoothness from adding it just beyond. I did have to make a few adjustments to this recipe--mainly to the crust and the strawberry filling. I only used 1/4 tsp cinnamon and 2 tbsps sugar in the crust; and I prebaked it for 15 minutes at 350. I let it cool, and then poured the cheesecake filling on it. I would definitely do that again, as the crust came out perfectly, with no sogginess. As for the strawberry filling: made as written, it didn't work for me. The strawberry sauce was far too thick, and no amount of water would thin it enough. So I made a different version: I placed a couple cups of unsweetened frozen sliced strawberries, a little sugar, and some lemon juice in a saucepot over medium heat. Once the strawberries defrosted all the way, I mashed them with a potato masher, then pressed the mixture through a fine mesh strainer. I poured the strained juice back into the pot, and added a corn starch slurry of 1 TEASPOON corn starch mixed with a bit of water. Stirred that into the strawberry juice and let that boil until slightly thickened. That worked much better as a strawberry filling for me. I followed the cheesecake portion of the recipe (and the baking of it) exactly as the recipe stated. I love love love the result! Beautiful, stunning, amazing, delicious cheesecake! Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Too many have made this and raved over it but mine cracked horribly as it cooled. But it looks pretty, has an amazing flavor and a nice creamy texture as compared to most. I agree with one reader, 1 tsp of cinnamon in the crust is plenty.

I make cheesecakes all the time but mine take 5 hours in a low oven of 200°F. They come out so creamy and stay flat. I have to give this 4 stars because it took forever for the center to even get close to setting which is 163°F (allows for carry-over baking to reach 165°F). After an hour, a test probe far from center came out wet. After that I used a digital thermometer. My oven is calibrated and spot on regarding baking temperatures.

On a positive ending note, I like the technique of the swirl in the center (I'm just not creative at all), and the sauce. I used fresh strawberries and sweetened them to just slightly tart to contrast with the sweetness of the custard. 

So, in all fairness, I'll try this recipe again only in a low, 200°F oven for 4 - 5 hours and see how it works regarding appearance - flavor-wise this is delicious! Win some - lose some. Never say die!

Friends raved over the crust. I made in a cupcake tin and formed a dense crust by placing a tbsp of crust mix in each cup and pressed the mix down using a 1/4 cup sized measuring cup. Still chilled it but used a 1/3 cup sized of batter in each cup and layered the top w fruit puree. Baked for 20-25 just until the cheesecake set. Was great for single serve portions.

The recipe is fairly vague when it comes to cooking, and when you should pull the cheesecake out. Plus, I would add that you should put a cookie sheet underneath the Cheesecake in the oven, to catch any melted butter from the pan. Also, unless you have a convection oven, you need to turn the cake about every 10 minutes to ensure an even bake.
When it comes to separating the cake from the spring-form pan, use a hot knife first, then go back for a second time and just run a plastic knife around the edge to be sure.
All things considered, it is a fairly good recipe.

not bad however I suggest make the puree differently, put it frozen strawberries, 2 tbsp of sugar and a squeeze of lemon on a pot and mash or blend once soft with a tbsp or cornstarch. Optionally put back on heat. Personally worked way better than how it says on recipe and I’ve made this 3 times.

It turned out great. But for me I didn’t add the eggs and lemon juice and just baked it for 10 minutes at 300 degrees. It still turned out really good because I froze it before serving which makes the crust more crunchy. Also I added a bit less sugar in the crust because for my crust I used a sweeter biscuit. But overall this is a great recipe!
I used sweet canned cherries instead of strawberrys and poured it on top instead of swirling. It was a simple, easy recipe and it was really good. Not to sweet.

This is my fave strawberry cheesecake! I use fresh berries and add a touch of Splenda instead of using frozen, sweetened berries. For a thinner crust, I crush a few almond cookies in a blender, spray my spring form pan with Pam, add the cookie crumbs to the pan, then tap them to cover the bottom and sides. That adds just enough of a 'crust' for us. It also makes a pretty presentation when the cheesecake peeks through the crumbs. I'll be serving this cheesecake for our anniversary!
I like this recipe but I only had fresh strawberries, so I used about 2 lbs of berries and added 1/2 cup sugar along with the other ingredients in the sauce. It turned out very pretty!

This was a great recipe! Using this every time I have the urge to bake. Everyone loved it! I didn’t have condensed milk on hand so I used 1 cup of sour cream with 3/4 cup of granulated sugar and it came out great! This is considered a great substitution after doing some quick research. Thanks for sharing this recipe!!
It’s great would use it again.
I didn't make any changes. Made it for a friend 25th birthday.
Stick to the recipe and it will be a hit. First time made it and was a hit. Thank you!

I’ve made this cheesecake twice a year, every year - for my stepdaughter’s birthday and for Christmas, for the last 8 years! Everyone loves it! Sometimes I make swirls with the strawberries, but sometimes I use them to “write” my daughter’s age on top for her birthday or draw a Christmas themed picture for Christmas. I’m not very artistic so you wouldn’t be able to sell it in a store, but it’s fun to do!

I followed the recipe and had way too much filling. Even if I used a 10" cake pan, it would have been too much. So much that I put the extra cream cheese & strawberry sauce in a ceramic casserole dish and baked it alongside the cheesecake. If I used 2/3 of the ingredients as listed it would have been just right for a 9" pie.
Excellent recipe! I didn’t layer the strawberry, I made raspberry coulis hearts instead, but the actual cheesecake tasted just how we love it!
It turned out perfect!
This was my first time ever making cheesecake and it was so easy to make! It turned out so good and the strawberry sauce is amazing!

Tastes great! First time making a cheesecake and this recipe was an easy first! I did however have to make double the crust to even get anywhere full on my pie dish. And I also had way too much cheesecake batter and strawberry sauce. Had to bake mine for about 65 minutes to set. Guess I'll just make more crust and make little muffin-sized cheesecakes with the extras. Would make again, with these tweaks.
